To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) exposure to high psychological demand and to low decision latitude decreased slightly between 2002-2004, but that exposure to intimidation and harassment increased substantially; 2) exposure to high levels of job strain and to poor social support was associated with psychological distress in 2004; 3) exposure to low reward was also associated with psychological distress; and 4) exposure to intimidation and psychological harassment were associated with psychological distress.

in the absence or specific organizational intervention aimed to improve the work situation, correctional officers are still more likely to experience high psychological demands and poor decision latitude than the general population of workers in contact with the general public in Quebec.
the psychosocial work environment of correctional officers remains poor, and that the prevalence of interpersonal violence at work increased substantially.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the psychosocial environment of correctional officers and the effects of this environment on the health and well-being of these officers.
the psychosocial work environment of correctional officers and the effects of this work environment on the mental health of these officers.
the psychosocial work environment and interpersonal violence at the workplace of correctional officers, and the consequences for their mental health.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
correctional officers in Canada, in Quebec, and in the United States, experience higher levels of stress than the general population.

in the absence, in the correctional milieu, of a preventive organizational intervention aimed at reducing the psychosocial constraints of the work environment and the interpersonal violence at work, correctional officers continue to be exposed to a high level of psychosocial risks and interpersonal violence at the work place.
the psychosocial constraints, interpersonal violence and mental health of correctional officers have not improved over the years.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the psychosocial work environment is a major determinant of psychological health among correctional workers and that the prevalence of exposure to psychosocial constraints at work has not changed between 2002-2004.

the correctional officers in the Quebec correctional system are exposed to a work environment that is highly stressful, characterized by high psychological demands, little decision latitude and poor support from colleagues and superiors, and by high levels of intimidation at work.

the psychosocial work environment of correctional officers is characterized by high psychological demands, a lack of control over one's work, and an imbalance between effort at work and reward, which is a source of stress for correctional officers.
The main takeaway from our work is that

correctional officers are exposed to a psychosocial work environment and interpersonal violence at the workplace that is particularly deleterious to their health, and that the situation is getting worse.
correctional officers are exposed to psychosocial constraints that are more severe than those of other workers and to high levels of violence at work.

correctional officers working in Quebec are exposed to a work situation which is characterized by a high level of psychosocial demands, low decision-making latitude, poor social support from colleagues and supervisors, poor reward at work, an imbalance between effort at work and reward and a high rate of intimidation.
